extracted.intended_audience: creative writing workshop participants (students, authors, instructors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for giving and receiving peer critiques of fiction manuscripts in a workshop setting, covering what to evaluate (plot, character, setting, craft), how to behave as a critic, and typical workshop procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the story's narrative structure and causal progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Inciting incident clear? Rising action present? Climax earned? Pacing across the piece? Stakes evident? Causality vs. coincidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterization
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the believability, distinctiveness, and development of characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Protagonist 3D? Multiple characters distinguishable? Believable motivation? Growth/transformation arc?

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge how place and sensory detail are used and how setting affects the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Place rendered specifically? Sensory grounding? Setting affects events/character? Internal consistency?

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic of the Underlying Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the internal consistency and coherence of the story's premise and world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Premise consistent? World rules followed? Plot holes?

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of Opening
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the opening hooks the reader and establishes appropriate entry into the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Hook present? Establishes voice? Promises the right thing? Right entry point chosen?

rubrics_metrics.name: Effectiveness of Ending
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the ending is justified by the story and provides satisfying resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Questions to address: Earned? Resonant? Surprising-yet-inevitable? Resolves what was raised?

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of Storytelling
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate scenecraft, narrative voice, point of view, and sentence-level prose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aspects to consider: POV control; Voice consistency; Scene vs. summary balance; Show vs. tell; Dialogue authenticity; Sentence-level prose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critic's Role (do not rewrite)
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary ethic for a critic: help the author realize their vision rather than rewrite the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: 'The critic's job is not to rewrite but to help the author realize their vision' — i.e., help them create the piece the way they envision it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance in Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure critiques include both positive observations and constructive criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: Balance — say positive things alongside criticism; 'writers often don't know what they're doing right'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity of Comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer concrete, text-anchored feedback over vague generalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: Specific, not vague — point to specific lines/scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructive Orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer suggestions and possibilities, not only problem identification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: Constructive, not just identifying problems — suggest possibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Silence Rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A procedural norm about author participation during critique discussions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: Author silence rule (Iowa workshop tradition) — author often doesn't speak during their critique; absorbs feedback. (Author may have final word at end per format.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on Process and Craft (not personal taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep critique grounded in craft and process rather than asserting personal taste as verdict.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guideline text: Process- and craft-focused — not personal taste assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript Distribution and Length Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural expectation about how submissions are circulated and typical length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical: Manuscript distributed in advance (typically 20–30 pages).

rubrics_metrics.name: Written Reader Feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that workshop participants prepare written notes in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical: All readers prepare written feedback to bring to the discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion Timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Typical duration of in-class discussion for a single manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical: 15–45 minute discussion in class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instructor's Role in Discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructor synthesizes and extends peer feedback during or after the discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical: Instructor synthesizes/extends discussion and may guide revision priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author Revision Expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectation that the author will revise the piece informed by workshop feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical: Author revises based on feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission Earns Close Attention
rubrics_metrics.description: An implicit criterion: a 'good' submission is one that attracts sustained, careful reading and discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit Criteria from the Workshop Model: 'Earns close attention'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear Craft Choices to Discuss
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion that submissions should present discernible craft decisions that can be talked about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit Criteria from the Workshop Model: 'Has clear craft choices to discuss.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveals Authorial Vision/Intent
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion that the manuscript should show some sense of the author's aims or voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit Criteria from the Workshop Model: 'Reveals authorial vision/intent.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient Technical Competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion that the work be technically competent enough to allow focus on higher-level concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit Criteria from the Workshop Model: 'Is technically competent enough to focus on higher-level concerns.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to Take Risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Implicit criterion valuing boldness: the piece should take risks that open useful critical territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicit Criteria from the Workshop Model: 'Is bold enough to risk failure.'
